note: AWK-64's transcription of the three scanned Tilles Center LIYO programs,
separated from the script that applies it. Read by transcribe_programs.py,
asserted by tilles-center-programs.test.ts.
DECIDED AND NEVER REGENERATED, in the sense period-and-forms.json uses. The
sources are three image-only scans in docs/archive/ and nothing derives this
file -- there is no parser to re-run, because the programs are in no
spreadsheet and no graph. Re-reading them means rendering them by eye. So a
correction here is the only record of the correction, and a re-run of the
applier must not overwrite one.
WHY A DECLARATION AT ALL, when AWK-59 transcribed 1993-07-26 by hand and
committed only docs: 35 entries went into the live space that day and the
repository holds no statement of what they were. The prose in
participation-checklist.md is a summary, not a manifest -- it cannot be
diffed against the space, and nothing fails if the two disagree. This file
can be, and the test does.
THE ONE THING THAT WILL SURPRISE WHOEVER READS THE TICKET FIRST: AWK-64 says
'create the 17 Works'. Eleven of the seventeen already exist. Works are
shared across Concerts -- the space holds 649 of them for 253 Concerts -- so
creating seventeen would have produced eleven duplicates, and one of those
would have failed the build. `reuse.works` is therefore load-bearing, not a
convenience: see the comment on that object.
PROGRAM WORDING LIVES ON THE ITEM, NOT ON THE WORK. ADR-0006 makes a Work
the composition as performed and AWK-64 says to keep the program's own
wording, but a reused Work already carries a title written for another
concert. Both rules hold at once because app/lib/archive.ts resolves an
item's display string as `item.fields.label ?? work.fields.title` -- so the
label is the per-performance string and the place the printed wording goes.
That is why item 1 of 1992-12-13 reads 'Carneval Overture' while the Work it
links stays 'Carnival Overture'. The scan says Carneval; the archive has
said Carnival since the import; neither is corrected to match the other.
New Work titles keep the program's wording with ONE normalisation: `#N`
becomes `No. N`, because all 649 live titles use `No.` and the `#` is a
typewriter convention rather than a different name. It affects exactly one
new title, Hungarian Rhapsody No. 1, whose printed form survives on the
item label anyway.
PERIOD AND FORM ARE DELIBERATELY ABSENT from the two new Composers and the
six new Works. ADR-0007 puts every form judgement in period-and-forms.json
and lets Form stay incomplete -- 'a Work with no form tags is not a defect'
-- so assigning forms here would open a second home for a decision that
already has one. Period arrives on its own: seed_period_and_forms.py is
idempotent, the new Concerts pull Piston, Ferdinand David and Franck into
scope, and work.period inherits from the composer in the sweep (AWK-37).
Run imslp_harvest.py then seed_period_and_forms.py after applying this.
CONDUCTOR SLUGS ARE NULL, against the letter of the ticket's checklist. All
46 live conductors have conductor.slug unset, no route reads it, and the
only thing that touches it is AWK-61's whitespace invariant. Slugging two of
forty-eight would leave a partial state for someone to explain later.
Decided by Alex on 2026-08-31.
Two pages each, image-only, no text layer. Recompressed to JPEG at 2200px
on the way in under 640f723 and legible; do not re-scan. Page 1 of each is
the title page (season, date, hall, conductor, soloists), page 2 the
program. Read them by extracting the embedded DCTDecode streams -- the
pages ARE JPEGs, so no renderer is needed and none is installed here.
Live entry ids this transcription links but does not create. Every one was
verified present on 2026-08-31 before the ids were written down.
THE NAMES BESIDE THE IDS ARE A CHECK, NOT A LABEL. transcribe_programs.py
re-reads each entry and aborts if the id has gone missing, if it now
resolves to a different content type, or if its live name no longer
matches what is recorded here -- the same checked redundancy
seed_period_and_forms.py keeps over its curated work ids. So correcting a
name here is not tidying; it is the thing that keeps the check honest.
The test can only assert these are non-empty and well-formed, because it
has no network.

franck.why: Was `Franck, Cesar` when this file was written, and the pre-flight's RENAMED check caught it. The period seed restored the diacritic the same day, because these three Concerts are what first brought Franck into scope at all -- so the accented form is what the space now holds and what this must match. His slug is untouched and still folds to `franck-cesar`, per ADR-0008.

note: The eleven the ticket would have duplicated. `why` records the
identification, because three of them are not a title match and a later
reader is entitled to know how the program's line was resolved.
The Tchaikovsky entry is the one that matters most. AWK-64 flags
'Theme and variations from Suite #3' as a slug-collision risk against the
existing Tchaikovsky suites and says to check (composer, slug) before
writing. The check's answer is that the work is not a near-miss, it is
the SAME work: AWK-59 created it for the 1993-07-26 program, which
printed the same excerpt. Reuse is what the warning was pointing at.
Writing a second record would have collided on
(cmp-tchaikovsky-pyotr-ilyich, theme-and-variations-from-suite-no-3) and
failed work-slug-unique-per-composer at build time -- the guard that
replaced work.slug's unique constraint when AWK-37 dropped it.

norfolk-rhapsody.title: Norfolk Rhapsody No. 1

franck-symphony.title: Symphony in D Minor

leonore-3.title: Leonore Overture No. 3
leonore-3.why: Printed 'Leonore Overture # 3, opus 72a'. The opus number is the same work's; it survives on the label.

romeo-and-juliet.title: Fantasy Overture, Romeo and Juliet
romeo-and-juliet.why: Printed 'Overture - Fantasy "Romeo and Juliet"'. Same work, words reversed.

merry-wives.title: Overture, The Merry Wives of Windsor
merry-wives.why: Printed 'Overture to "The Merry Wives of Windsor"'. Nicolai's only work in the archive.

mozart-violin-5.title: Violin Concerto No. 5 in A Major
mozart-violin-5.why: Printed 'Violin Concerto #5 (first movement)'. The complete work is reused and the item carries the qualification in its note -- Alex's call on 2026-08-31, over the alternative of a separate ', mvt I' Work. The space holds five such single-movement Works, so both readings had a precedent.

weber-bassoon.title: Bassoon Concerto in F Major
weber-bassoon.why: Printed 'Bassoon Concerto #1 (first movement)'. Weber wrote one bassoon concerto and the archive holds it under its key rather than a number, so '#1' and 'in F Major' are the same piece. First movement only, noted on the item.

theme-and-variations.title: "Theme and Variations", from Suite No. 3 in G Major
theme-and-variations.why: Printed 'Theme and variations from Suite #3'. AWK-59 created this record for the 1993-07-26 program's item 13. See this object's note.

espana.title: Espana
espana.why: Printed '"Espana" Rhapsody'. The archive already tags it forms: ['Rhapsody'], so the printed word is the form, not part of the name. Chabrier's only work in the archive.

note: The two AWK-64 found absent, confirmed absent again on 2026-08-31 across
all 259 live Composers. Neither carries dates: the programs print none,
and this file records what the scans say.
`period` is absent on purpose -- see the top note. Both have IMSLP pages,
so imslp_harvest.py should reach them.

cmp-david-ferdinand.why: Not to be confused with the three live Composers a search for 'David' finds: Earnest, John David; Davidson, Charles; and Willcocks, David (arr.).

note: Both were Associate Conductor -- Deaver in 1992-93, Stickley in 1994-95 --
and each took exactly one item, which is the whole reason AWK-60 built
programItem.conductor. `slug` is deliberately absent; see the top note.
Five student soloists, none of them live. Every instrument here is already
in the space's vocabulary (Piano 23, Violin 26, Bassoon 8, Flute 6,
Trombone 6), so none introduces a new spelling. soloist.fullName is
space-wide unique and all five were free.
Instruments come from each program's title page, which lists them; the
program page names the soloist without the instrument.
The six genuinely new Works. Slugs are hand-written per ADR-0008 -- the
importer's hashed form is not an address anyone should ship -- and each was
checked against its composer's live slugs and against both patterns
app/lib/invariants.ts rejects. None contains `--`; none ends in six hex
characters (the near-miss shape that catches a title whose last word is
six letters from a-f).
`period` and `forms` are absent on purpose. See the top note.

wrk-marche-ecossaise.title: Marche Ecossaise
wrk-marche-ecossaise.why: Printed without accents, and kept that way -- the archive's other Debussy titles are unaccented too (Prelude a l'apres midi d'un faune, Danse Sacree et Danse Profane). AWK-37 restored diacritics to composer NAMES, not to work titles.

wrk-symphonic-metamorphosis-on-themes-of.why: Hindemith's second work in the archive; the first is Nobilissima Visione. The title names Weber but the composer is Hindemith.

wrk-hungarian-rhapsody-no-1.title: Hungarian Rhapsody No. 1
wrk-hungarian-rhapsody-no-1.why: Printed 'Hungarian Rhapsody #1'; normalised to `No.` per the top note. The archive already holds No. 2, as 'Hungarian Rhapsody No. 2 in D Minor'.

note: Movements for a Work that already exists, kept apart from `works` because
the applier's semantics differ: this is a merge into an empty field on a
live record, not a creation. Franck's Symphony in D Minor holds movement:
[] today and the 1992-12-13 program prints all three, so the scan supplies
something the archive lacks.
The applier writes this ONLY into an empty field. import_to_contentful.py
names movement lists as curated data it must never overwrite, and a
transcription is in no position to disagree with a curator.
Ids, titles and item ids follow AWK-59's 1993-07-26 exactly: cnc-YYYYMMDD,
a title of 'YYYY-MM-DD — LIYO' with an em dash, and pi-YYYYMMDD-N ordered
from 1. Program items are created fresh per Concert and never shared --
app/lib/invariants.ts fails a build where one item sits on two Concerts
more than 14 days apart, because a program item is one performance.
attended is true on all three and satOut is empty on all three: Alex
played every item of every one, stated 2026-08-31. Unlike 1993-07-26,
these programs carry no visiting ensemble's blocks, so there is nothing
for satOut to hold.
`conductor` is Dreiwitz on all three, and the two items he did not take
carry their own.
`sourceNote` IS NOT WRITTEN TO CONTENTFUL, and that is not an oversight.
Each program's title page states which concert of which season it is and
that it began at 7:30 on a Sunday evening; the content model has nowhere to
put any of it. `concert.dateNote` exists but qualifies a DATE, and filling
it with a start time would be a misuse that then renders. So the fact is
kept here, in the committed record, and nowhere else -- exactly what AWK-59
did with Keith Glover compering on 1993-07-26.
It is worth knowing because the season ordinals are the corroboration:
'first concert of the 1992-93 season' and '32nd Season' are how these dates
were assigned to sea-liyo-30 and sea-liyo-32 rather than guessed from the
year, and CONTEXT.md's LIYO numbering agrees from the other direction. The
test asserts all three carry one, so the key cannot quietly rot into the
dead weight it would otherwise look like.
NO ITEM CARRIES `character`, AND ADDING ONE BACK WOULD BE A MISTAKE. The
field holds the non-instrument role a performer took -- the space's honest
examples are `Isolde`, `Dancer` and `Filmmaker` -- which is what
parse_archive.py means by it: the credit left over once the instrument
enumeration has claimed everything it recognises. An instrument belongs on
`soloist.instrument`, where these five already carry it.
The first version of this file set `character` to the instrument on all
five, copying AWK-59's `pi-19930726-12`. That was the wrong precedent to
copy, and the audit that found it also found the corpus half-agreed: of the
seven live values predating this ticket, four were instruments or voice
types and three were roles. Alex chose on 2026-08-31 to make the field mean
one thing, so these five were cleared AND so was AWK-59's -- a one-off
correction outside this transcription, recorded here because it is the only
place that explains why `pi-19930726-12` changed under a different ticket's
name. The instrument is not lost: it is on the soloist, and in `credits`.
The test asserts no item here carries the field.
